dedupe_keys.name: planning for resilience of water networks under earthquake hazard rotorua district new zealand gns science

description: This case study by GNS Science researchers applies a transparent three-step risk assessment to the water supply and wastewater networks of Rotorua Lakes Council in New Zealand. The steps are to define an earthquake scenario, identify the vulnerable network components, and estimate likely outage time of services, with ground motion intensity estimation, damage identification and outage modelling affected by the number of repair crews and preferred repair strategies. It responds to New Zealand statutory duties on network providers to manage natural hazard risk and to the lessons of the Canterbury earthquakes, and follows a 2018 GNS consultancy report implementing RiskScape for the council. Coverage: one district's supply and wastewater assets under a scenario earthquake. Access: a free journal article; the licence is not stated on the page read. Caveats: results depend on the chosen scenario and asset data, and only the abstract and references were read here. It is intended as an example for other councils and supports hazard exposure, restoration and emergency response planning, and relates to the RiskScape platform and the earthquake repair strategy case study in the catalogue.
